## Context / Problem
Operators need an authoritative configuration precedence/source/lifecycle reference and a security reference that stay byte-current with the config schema and the deprecation/secret-name registries rather than drifting by hand. The existing `docs/config.md` is a 648-line HAND-AUTHORED operator doc (rationale, precedence narrative, a `## Config-key inventory`, a `### Secrets` list, the `## ticket.default_assignee` section, a fail-loud tombstone-registry section, stable anchor slugs) with many in-repo consumers: content-asserting tests (`test_snapshot_docs.py`, `test_session_id.py`, `test_structured_run.py`, `test_harness_provenance.py`, `test_session_shims.py`, `test_agents_claim_assignee_guidance.py`, `test_build_drift.py`, `test_llm_model_env_removal.py`), anchor deep links (`AGENTS.md#ticketdefault_assignee`, `docs/reuse-surface.md#rebar_operation_snapshot_shadow`, `docs/concurrency.md#config-key-inventory`),. Byte-generating into `config.md` would strand these consumers.

## Outcome
A new `scripts/gen_config_reference.py` generates a NEW standalone, fully-generated `docs/config-reference.md` (the machine-current, registry-derived precedence/source/lifecycle reference) and a NEW indexed `docs/security.md`. Its concrete inputs are three symbols: the typed config schema `rebar._config_schema` (keys/types/defaults), `rebar._deprecations.REGISTRY` + `rebar._deprecations.tombstones()` filtered to `kind=="cfg"` (the per-key LIFECYCLE/deprecation/removal column — a NEW cfg-channel derivation modelled on how `gen_env_registry.py` reads `kind=="env"` entries), and `rebar._child_env._ADAPTER_SECRET_NAMES` (the secret-name inventory). There is no discrete "ownership registry" (ownership is a DERIVED AST classification in `scripts/check_config_ownership.py`); the generator does NOT read it. `docs/config.md` is LEFT ENTIRELY UNCHANGED, so all its consumers stay intact by construction. Non-registry-derivable narrative topics named by the epic (precedence rule, observability exception, subprocess limitations, behavior deltas, native refresh) are supplied VERBATIM from a curated template constant in the generator, not synthesized. `docs/README.md` and `docs/architecture.md` navigation reference the new docs. A newline-normalizing `--check` drift mode, gated by a pytest suite (run under `make test`, no CI dependency), fails when either generated doc is stale.

## Plan
1. Add `scripts/gen_config_reference.py` (modelled on `gen_env_registry.py`/`gen_cli_reference.py`): read `rebar._config_schema` (keys/types/defaults), `rebar._deprecations.REGISTRY` + `rebar._deprecations.tombstones()` (`kind=="cfg"` → lifecycle column), and `rebar._child_env._ADAPTER_SECRET_NAMES` (secret-name inventory), and render (a) registry-derived tables and (b) the curated template constant (the precedence/observability/subprocess/behavior-delta/native-refresh narrative, verbatim) into fully-generated `docs/config-reference.md` and `docs/security.md`. Both are generated whole (no partial-region markers — new generator-owned files). Each carries a top-of-file markdown banner within its first 8 lines containing the word "generated" AND the exact command `python scripts/gen_config_reference.py`, per `test_generated_surface_markers.py::test_text_surface_carries_a_banner`. The generator exposes `main(["--check"])` returning 0 when the committed docs match and nonzero on drift (as `gen_cli_reference.py`/`gen_env_registry.py` do).
2. Create `docs/config-reference.md` and `docs/security.md`; update `docs/README.md` and `docs/architecture.md` navigation. Register BOTH docs in the parity gate: add each (→ `python scripts/gen_config_reference.py`) to the `GENERATED` map in `tests/unit/test_generated_surface_markers.py`, AND add a matching row for each to the `### Generated — never edit these by hand` TABLE in `docs/README.md` — the table row set must EQUAL `GENERATED`+`GATED_HAND_AUTHORED` (`test_readme_table_matches_registry`), so the prose nav link is not sufficient. Do NOT modify `docs/config.md`.
3. Add pytest suite `tests/unit/test_gen_config_reference.py` (modelled on `tests/unit/test_gen_cli_reference.py`) that asserts `gen.main(["--check"]) == 0` on the committed docs and drives the topic/preservation/newline coverage below. This is the DRIFT GATE and it runs under `make test` — portable, no CI provider required; `--check` compares with newline normalization (universal-newline / text-mode read, not raw byte compare) so a CRLF autocrlf checkout does not false-fail.

## Testing (RED -> GREEN)
- Drift: a deliberate edit to either generated file makes `gen.main(["--check"])` return nonzero; regenerating clears it.
- Preservation (by construction): `docs/config.md` is byte-unchanged, proven by a test asserting the generator/`--check` never target `config.md`; its content-asserting suites named in Context continue to pass.
- Topic coverage: a test asserts that, across `docs/config-reference.md` and `docs/security.md` together, a heading/anchor exists for every entry in an explicit REQUIRED_TOPICS list — precedence, source, lifecycle, restart/redeploy rotation, native refresh, observability exception, subprocess limitations, behavior deltas, MCP/CLI exposure — failing if any is missing.
- Newline safety: a regression test feeds CRLF-encoded checked-out content while the generator emits LF and asserts `--check` reports NO drift.
- Parity gate: `tests/unit/test_generated_surface_markers.py` passes — each new doc carries its self-announcing banner (`test_text_surface_carries_a_banner`) and the `docs/README.md` table row set equals the registry (`test_readme_table_matches_registry`).
- Portability: the generator and its `--check` drift gate run under `make test` with no CI provider present.

## Compatibility / rollback
Docs-and-tooling only; no product-behavior change. `docs/config.md` and all its consumers are untouched. Rollback removes the generator (with its `--check` mode), the curated template constant, `docs/config-reference.md`, `docs/security.md`, `tests/unit/test_gen_config_reference.py`, the two `GENERATED`-map/README-table registrations, and reverts the two navigation edits.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `scripts/gen_config_reference.py` generates `docs/config-reference.md` and `docs/security.md` whole from `rebar._config_schema`, `rebar._deprecations.REGISTRY`+`tombstones()` (cfg lifecycle), and `rebar._child_env._ADAPTER_SECRET_NAMES`, plus a curated template constant, and never writes `docs/config.md`.
- [x] `docs/config.md` is byte-unchanged and all its enumerated consumers remain intact (its content-asserting suites pass; its anchor slugs still resolve), proven by a test that the generator/`--check` do not target `config.md`.
- [x] Across `docs/config-reference.md` and `docs/security.md`, an anchor exists for every topic in the REQUIRED_TOPICS list (precedence, source, lifecycle, restart/redeploy rotation, native refresh, observability exception, subprocess limitations, behavior deltas, MCP/CLI exposure), proven by a topic-coverage test.
- [x] `docs/config-reference.md` carries a top-of-file banner (within its first 8 lines) naming `python scripts/gen_config_reference.py`, and `docs/security.md` carries the same, satisfying `test_generated_surface_markers.py::test_text_surface_carries_a_banner`.
- [x] Both new docs are registered in the `GENERATED` map of `tests/unit/test_generated_surface_markers.py` and in the `docs/README.md` `### Generated — never edit these by hand` table, so `test_readme_table_matches_registry` passes.
- [x] `gen.main(["--check"])` returns 0 on committed docs and nonzero on a stale doc, is exercised by `tests/unit/test_gen_config_reference.py` under `make test` with no CI dependency, and does NOT false-fail on a CRLF checkout (newline-normalized comparison).
- [x] `docs/README.md` and `docs/architecture.md` navigation reference the new docs.
